item.title: On the Hodge Extension of Local K\"ahler Forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.38055v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X$ be a Stein manifold, and let $K=\{h\le0\}$ be a compact sublevel set of a strictly plurisubharmonic function $h$ defined near $K$. It is known that $K$ is meromorphically convex in $X$ if and only if $dd^ch$ extends to a Hodge form on $X$. We show that if $H_2(X,\mathbb Z)$ is the direct sum of a free abelian group and a torsion group, for example if it is finitely generated, then any extension of $dd^ch$ to a K\"ahler form on $X$ can be modified, after replacing $h$ by a positive multiple, into a Hodge form. Thus meromorphic convexity of $K$ is equivalent to the extendability of $dd^ch$ as a K\"ahler form. We also show that the topological assumption cannot be dropped: we construct a Stein manifold $X$ of dimension $6$ with $H_2(X,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Q$, a sublevel set $K$ as above that is not meromorphically convex although $dd^ch$ extends to a K\"ahler form, and a totally real torus in $K$ that is isotropic for a K\"ahler form but is not meromorphically convex. This shows that the Hodge condition in Guedj's characterization of meromorphically convex totally real submanifolds cannot be weakened to a K\"ahler condition, and gives counterexamples to two criteria stated by Cieliebak and Eliashberg.
item.dc:creator: Rasul Shafikov

item.title: Meromorphic solutions of a nonlinear differential-difference equation with two exponential terms
item.description: arXiv:2610.38247v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $n\geq 2$ and $k\geq 1$ be integers. We study finite order meromorphic solutions of the nonlinear differential-difference equation \begin{equation*} f^{n}(z)f'(z)+P_{d}(z,f)=p_{1}(z){\rm e}^{\alpha_{1}z^{k}}+p_{2}(z){\rm e}^{\alpha_{2}z^{k}}, \end{equation*} where $P_{d}(z,f)\not\equiv 0$ is a difference polynomial in $f$ of degree $d\leq n-1$ whose coefficients are small meromorphic functions with respect to $f$, $p_{1},~p_{2}$ are nonzero meromorphic functions with $T(r,p_{j})=o(r^{k})$, $j=1,2$, and $\alpha_{1}\neq\alpha_{2}$ are nonzero constants. We prove that every such solution has order exactly $k$, and obtain sufficient conditions on $n,~d,~k$ for the equation to admit no finite order meromorphic solution with $N(r,\frac{1}{f})=S(r,f)$. Our results extend the known ones from linear exponents $z$ to polynomial exponents $z^{k}$, and replace the linear difference polynomials with the degree restriction $d\leq n-2$ assumed in the literature by general ones of degree $d\leq n-1$. Examples show that the restrictions on $n$ and $d$ are sharp.
item.dc:creator: Minfeng Chen, Zongsheng Gao

item.title: Nevanlinna Theory on Berkovich Curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.38435v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a value distribution theory for finite analytic morphisms between proper connected quasi-smooth Berkovich curves over a complete algebraically closed non-Archimedean field. The central tool is a multi-tail Dirichlet Green function on finite truncations of a generalized skeleton, which makes non-Archimedean potential theory on skeleta compatible with global Nevanlinna asymptotics. Using it, we prove the first main theorem as an exact identity relating the characteristic, counting, and proximity functions. For logarithmic targets we establish a second main theorem in both ramified and level-one truncated forms. The defect relation is also given. The theory provides a Berkovich-analytic framework for non-Archimedean value distribution, bridging classical Nevanlinna theory and its $p$-adic counterpart.
item.dc:creator: Tingbin Cao, Jiahu Peng

item.title: On a family of domains associated with $\mu$-synthesis in $M_2(\mathbb C)$
item.description: arXiv:2610.38677v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we show that the domain $\mathbb H$ serves as a unifying domain for $\mathbb G_2, \mathbb E$ and $\mathbb P$ by proving that each of these domains is an analytic retract of $\mathbb H$. Further, we prove that the bidisc $\mathbb D^2$ and the Euclidean unit ball $\mathbb B_2$ are also analytic retracts of $\mathbb H$. Then the rational $\overline{\mathbb H}$-inner functions, i.e., the rational maps from $\mathbb D$ into $\overline{\mathbb H}$ whose boundary values lie in the distinguished boundary of $\mathbb H$, are characterized. Two different versions of Schwarz type lemma for $\mathbb H$ are established of which one provides a necessary and sufficient condition. Finally, capitalizing on the theory of $\mathbb H$, we present alternative proofs to a few known results on $\mathbb P$ from the literature.
item.dc:creator: Indranil Biswas, Sourav Pal, Nitin Tomar

item.title: Regular closedness off the real axis for root closures of bounded-height integer polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.38971v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For each integer $h\ge1$, let $Z_h$ be the closure in the complex plane of the roots of nonzero integer polynomials whose coefficients have absolute value at most $h$, with no degree restriction. We prove that $Z_h$ is regular closed off the real axis: every non-real point of $Z_h$ is a limit of interior points. The root-closure identification of Espigul\'e and Juher, for which we include a self-contained proof, shows that the same closure arises from monic polynomials and that outside the closed unit disc it is the connectedness locus of $h+1$ equally spaced collinear similarities. The main step proves that this locus is regular closed off the real axis; this was known for $h=1$ by Calegari, Koch and Walker, for $h\ge19$, and inside an explicit lens. The symmetry $z\mapsto1/z$ then gives the full-plane statement. The proof adapts the method of traps of Calegari, Koch and Walker, using a neighboring-piece criterion, short chains through consecutive digits, and Rouch\'e's theorem. We also classify the convex attractors.
item.dc:creator: Bernat Espigule

item.title: Hermitian Clifford Analysis on Euclidean Domains with Smooth and Fractal Boundaries: A Survey of Matrix Cauchy and Hilbert Transforms, Boundary Value Problems, Helmholtz-Type Dirac Operators and Duality
item.description: arXiv:2610.39087v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hermitian Clifford analysis is a refinement of Euclidean Clifford analysis obtained by imposing a complex structure on $\R^{2n}$ and considering the simultaneous null solutions (the $h$-monogenic functions) of two mutually adjoint Hermitian Dirac operators. This survey collects, in a unified notation and without proofs, the main results obtained along this line of research between 2008 and 2026. We review the matrix Borel--Pompeiu, Koppelman and Cauchy formulae, first for domains with Liapunov or Ahlfors--David regular boundary and then for Jordan domains whose boundary is fractal in the sense of Mandelbrot; the associated Cauchy transform, Hilbert transform, Hardy projections and their mapping properties, including H\"older norm estimates in terms of the $d$-sum of a Whitney decomposition; the jump decomposition, Dirichlet and Riemann boundary value problems in each setting, including the linear Riemann problems with variable circulant coefficients and their nonlinear counterparts. We also review a duality theory for the module of germs of $H$-monogenic matrix functions, together with its Euclidean model (the annihilators of harmonic differential forms) and its algebraic prerequisites (a Poincar\'e lemma and a Mittag--Leffler theorem for circulant matrices); the function theory associated with a Hermitian version of the Helmholtz equation, the corresponding $\bar\partial$-problem and its application to a formal two-dimensional Maxwell-type system; and finally, the parallel development in the quaternionic Hermitian setting, where four Dirac operators and circulant $(4\times 4)$ matrices take over.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Abreu-Blaya, Juan Bory-Reyes, Carlos Daniel Tamayo-Castro

item.title: The inverse problem for Julia limiting directions in the Eremenko--Lyubich class
item.description: arXiv:2610.39103v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the inverse problem for Julia limiting directions in the Eremenko-Lyubich class $\mathcal B$, which is the class of transcendental entire functions with a bounded set of singular values, and its meromorphic generalization $\mathcal B_{mer}$. Every nonempty compact subset of the circle can be the set of Julia limiting directions of an entire $f\in\mathcal B$. For finite unions of nondegenerate closed arcs, the corresponding $f\in\mathcal B$, even with every finite order at or above an explicit bound determined by the arc lengths, can be attained. We also refine the series construction of the latter two authors to obtain $f\in \mathcal B_{mer}$ with any prescribed order and the set of Julia limiting directions.
item.dc:creator: Jiaxing Huang, Jun Wang, Xiao Yao

item.title: Higher order Teodorescu transform in the theory of generalized partial-slice monogenic functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.39238v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the higher order Teodorescu transform in the context of generalized partial-slice monogenic functions. By introducing the generalized poly-partial-slice Cauchy kernel, we derive some integral formulas including higher order Borel-Pompeiu formula and Cauchy integral formula for generalized poly-partial-slice monogenic functions. Furthermore, we define the higher order Teodorescu transform in this context and establish its existence, continuity, and some mapping properties. These results extend classical integral methods in Clifford analysis to the generalized poly-partial-slice setting.
item.dc:creator: Manjie Hu, Chao Ding

item.title: Uniform estimates for complex Monge-Amp\`ere equations II: Hermitian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.39259v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish uniform estimates for degenerate complex Monge--Amp\`ere equations on compact Hermitian manifolds under weak Orlicz integrability assumptions on the densities. Our estimates apply uniformly to Hermitian metrics and to semipositive uniformly non-collapsing reference forms. For arbitrary big reference forms, we obtain uniform relative $L^\infty$-estimates with respect to the extremal function with minimal singularities, and establish continuity of the resulting solutions on the regular locus. As an application, we prove the existence of solutions with minimal singularities to degenerate complex Monge--Amp\`ere equations associated with big forms. The proofs combine local Orlicz estimates with pluripotential-theoretic envelope techniques and uniform control of the Monge--Amp\`ere masses, overcoming the lack of invariance of the total Monge--Amp\`ere mass in the Hermitian setting.
item.dc:creator: Quang-Tuan Dang, Lei Zhang, Bin Zhou

item.title: The functional analytic approach establishes the Corona theorem in the theory of SCV
item.description: arXiv:2610.39425v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give an affirmative solution of the original Corona problem (1962) for certain bounded pseudoconvex domains or polydomains in $\mathbb{C}^n$, including the balls and polydiscs, by using the Gleason solvability property of such domains for $H^\infty(G)$. In fact, we establish an equivalency of the Corona problem and Gleason's problem (1964) in the theory of several complex variables. Indeed, we extend our recent works on both problems based on the functional analytic approaches, and extend recent work of Clos, as well as apply the usual Banach algebra method. As an application, we establish the I. J. Schark's theorem for these $G$'s. We also obtain a welcome extension of a result of Krantz and Li (1995) for a bounded, strictly pseudoconvex domain in $\mathbb{C}^n$ with $C^3$ boundary.
item.dc:creator: S. R. Patel

item.title: Meromorphic order from Taylor coefficients, least singular values of Hankel matrices and rational approximants
item.description: arXiv:2610.39453v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a natural notion of generalized order for entire and meromorphic functions and express it in terms of their Taylor coefficients. More precisely, one formula uses the least singular values of Hankel matrices of the coefficients, and the other uses their determinants. These formulas generalize the classical coefficient formula for the order of entire functions and its extensions by Edrei and Sheremeta. The proof combines a theorem of Pommerenke with a bound for the Nevanlinna characteristic that results from a convergence theorem for rational approximants introduced by Prokhorov. We also characterize the largest class of growth scales for which the associated generalized order is well-behaved.
item.dc:creator: Kei Beauduin

item.title: $\mathrm{BMO}$ Domains and Quasicircles Associated with Zygmund Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.39567v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate graph domains and graph curves from the viewpoints of $\mathrm{BMOA}$, Zygmund regularity, and asymptotic geometry. First, we prove that every graph domain is a $\mathrm{BMO}$ domain, which provides a proof of a statement of Astala and Zinsmeister. We then use a Weierstrass-type function to construct a Bishop-Jones quasicircle that is asymptotically conformal but not asymptotically smooth. This example yields the strict inclusions \[ \mathrm{VMOA}(\mathbb H) \subsetneq \mathrm{BMOA}(\mathbb H)\cap B_0(\mathbb H), \qquad \mathrm{SS}(\mathbb R) \subsetneq \mathrm{SQS}(\mathbb R)\cap\mathrm{S}(\mathbb R). \] Finally, by a localized lacunary construction, we produce a compactly supported locally absolutely continuous function $f$ with $f'\in\mathrm{BMO}(\mathbb R)\setminus\mathrm{VMO}(\mathbb R)$ whose graph is an asymptotically conformal chord-arc curve that is not asymptotically smooth.
item.dc:creator: Katsuhiko Matsuzaki, Fei Tao

item.title: Characterizations of $\varphi$-inner uniform domains and $\varphi$-uniform domains in metric spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.39574v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study $\varphi$-uniform/-inner uniform domains in metric spaces. In our first main result, we establish quantitative characterizations of three different definitions of $\varphi$-uniformity/-inner uniformity in length spaces. In our second main result, we obtain a geometric sufficient condition of $\varphi$-uniform/-inner uniform domains in doubling length spaces, which extends the corresponding result of Guo-Huang-Wang [arXiv 2025] and Gao-Guo-Huang-Wang [arXiv 2025] for linear case.
item.dc:creator: Shu-Jing Gao, Miao He

item.title: Rigidity of K\"ahler-Finsler Metrics with Constant Radial Curvature
item.description: arXiv:2610.39989v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove that a smooth strongly pseudoconvex K\"ahler--Finsler metric $F$ satisfying the constant radial curvature condition \[ \Omega(\chi,\bar\chi)\chi=cF^2\chi, c\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}, \] is induced by a Hermitian K\"ahler metric of holomorphic sectional curvature $2c$. Under the Abate--Patrizio curvature symmetry \[ \langle\Omega(\cdot,\bar\chi)\chi,\chi\rangle =\langle\Omega(\chi,\bar\chi)\cdot,\chi\rangle, \] this result gives Hermitian rigidity for nonzero constant holomorphic sectional curvature and the classification of complete simply connected metrics of negative curvature. As an application, we show that the Kobayashi metric of a bounded strongly convex domain with smooth boundary is K\"ahler--Finsler if and only if the domain is biholomorphic to the unit ball. We also prove that the universal cover of a bounded strongly pseudoconvex domain $D $ with smooth boundary is biholomorphic to the unit ball if and only if its Kobayashi metric is a smooth strongly pseudoconvex K\"ahler--Finsler metric. Furthermore, we give two explicit examples to illustrate the distinction between the weakly K\"ahler--Finsler and K\"ahler--Finsler conditions.
item.dc:creator: Jinling Li, Longjie Li, Chunhui Qiu

item.title: Invariant probability measures on holomorphic functions on the unit disk
item.description: arXiv:2610.40057v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study probability measures on the space of holomorphic functions on the unit disk that are invariant under pre-composition by conformal automorphisms and give no mass to constant functions. We determine the slowest possible growth of functions supported by such measures. Let $M_f(R)$ denote the maximum modulus of $f$ on the hyperbolic ball of radius $R$ centered at the origin. We show that given a non-decreasing function $G:[1,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$, there exists an $\textrm{Aut}(\mathbb{D})$-invariant probability measure $\mu$ on $\textrm{Hol}(\mathbb{D}, \mathbb{C}) \setminus \{\textrm{constant functions} \}$ such that $\log^+ M_f(R)=O_f(G(R))$ for $\mu$ almost every $f$ if and only if $\int_1^\infty (R/G(R)) \, dR <\infty$. For the lower bound, we use a mass transport argument to show that almost every trajectory of the gradient flow of $\log |f|$ has finite energy. To establish sharpness, we construct holomorphic functions of slow growth on infinite Riemann surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Oleg Ivrii, Uri Kreitner

item.title: Optimal subtrees of finite metric graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.40168v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a metric graph analog of a classical extremal problem for Riemann surfaces studied by Teichm\"uller, Jenkins, Strebel, and others. In particular, we prove that on any finite metric graph with a marked point, there is a unique open subtree which maximizes a metric graph analog of the reduced modulus, and we also give an equivalent characterization of this optimal subtree in terms of balanced harmonic measures.
item.dc:creator: Levi Haunschmid-Sibitz, Fredrik Viklund, David Witt Nystr\"om

item.title: On a class of meromorphic functions with three singular values
item.description: arXiv:2610.40202v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a parametrization of the class of real meromorphic functions in the plane for which the preimage of $\{0,1,\infty\}$ is contained in the real line, and all singular values belong to $\{0,1,\infty\}$. As corollaries, we obtain a new parabolic type criterion and prove that all such functions are limits of rational functions of the same class.
item.dc:creator: Alexandre Eremenko

item.title: On the Converse of Shimoda's Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.40381v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Shimoda's theorem on the holomorphicity of a function $f(z,w)$ defined in a bidisc $U\times V=\left\{ \left| z \right|<1 \right\}\times \left\{ \left| w \right|<1 \right\},$ which is holomorphic with respect to $w\in V$ for each fixed $z\in U$ and is holomorphic with respect to $z\in U$ for each fixed $w\in E$, where $E\subset V$ is a countable set with at least one limit point in $V$. Shimoda proved that in this case $f(z,w)$ is holomorphic in $U\times V$ except for a nowhere dense closed subset of $U\times V$. We prove a converse: for any relatively closed nowhere dense set $S\subset U$ such that $\partial U\bigcup S$ is connected, there exists a function satisfying the conditions of Shimoda's theorem that is holomorphic in $(U\setminus S)\times V$ and doesn't extend holomorphically to any point of $S\times V$.
item.dc:creator: Sevdiyor Imomkulov, Kamol Rasulov

item.title: Calabi-Yau Hyperbolicity
item.description: arXiv:2610.37996v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The goal of this paper is to introduce a new notion of hyperbolicity for compact complex manifolds with trivial canonical bundle, called \textit{Calabi--Yau hyperbolicity}. We investigate its fundamental properties and establish a characterization in terms of the fundamental group. In particular, we show that no compact K\"ahler Calabi--Yau manifold is Calabi--Yau hyperbolic, highlighting the genuinely non-K\"ahler nature of this notion. We also investigate different techniques for constructing examples of such manifolds. Finally, we examine the relationship between Calabi--Yau hyperbolicity and Kobayashi hyperbolicity in the examples considered, highlighting obstructions to the latter in the Calabi--Yau setting.
item.dc:creator: Abdelouahab Khelifati

item.title: The Miyaoka-Yau inequality and the delta invariant for Fano varieties II -soliton case-
item.description: arXiv:2610.38137v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Inspired by recent work of Inoue and Hallam-Lahdili, we prove an equivariant Miyaoka-Yau inequality with a correction term for smooth Fano manifolds admitting K\"ahler-Ricci solitons. It recovers the usual Miyaoka-Yau inequality in the K\"ahler-Einstein case. Our proof uses weighted equivariant Bogomolov-Gieseker and Langer inequalities for torsion-free sheaves, together with a weighted slope estimate for the canonical extension sheaf. We also construct toric examples showing that the existence of a soliton implies neither weighted semistability of the canonical extension sheaf nor nonnegativity of the equivariant Miyaoka-Yau number.
item.dc:creator: Tomoyuki Hisamoto, Masataka Iwai

item.title: Spectral Structures on Vector Bundles
item.description: arXiv:2610.38972v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop an intrinsic theory of spectral structures on holomorphic vector bundles over compact Riemann surfaces, generalising eigenspace decompositions without eigenvalues. Their geometric realisations are presentations of vector bundles as pushforwards of line bundles along finite branched covers. We construct their analytic moduli stack locally of finite presentation and identify it with the relative Picard stack of the universal family of finite covers. We prove that the forgetful morphism to the stack of vector bundles is representable by analytic spaces and is smooth and surjective on a distinguished smooth open substack. Consequently, every holomorphic family of vector bundles locally admits spectral presentations along smooth connected simply branched covers, and these presentations can be deformed alongside the underlying bundles. The relative Picard description yields explicit local dimension formulas and recovers the stack of regular Higgs bundles as base change along the Hitchin base. We also characterise the additional data supplied to a spectral structure by a regular Higgs field as a global twisted generator, and give examples of smooth connected spectral structures which cannot arise from any Higgs field.
item.dc:creator: Nikita Nikolaev

item.title: Logarithmic transformations on the six-sphere
item.description: arXiv:2610.39102v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that there are infinitely many choices of the multiplicities in the logarithmic transformation step of the Alp\"oge--Claude construction which produce a complex threefold diffeomorphic to the six-sphere. Moreover, distinct choices of the multiplicities yield biholomorphically inequivalent complex structures.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Viaclovsky

item.title: Unified transform method for nonautonomous linear evolution equations: rigorous analysis and qualitative theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.39698v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Established herein is the rigorous extension of the celebrated Fokas unified transform method for linear evolution PDE with time-dependent coefficients. As illustrative examples, considered below and rigorously analysed in detail are non-homogeneous initial-boundary-value problems, formulated on the half-line, for the heat equation and the modified heat (also widely known as Barenblatt's pseudo-parabolic) equation with reaction terms and temporally varying coefficients. Solution formulae are derived formally via suitable implementation of the UTM, and rigorously verified a posteriori, in the classical sense. The latter task relies on complex-analytic tools and careful interpretation of the obtained integral representations. The explicit solutions established here are then used for investigating qualitative properties. These include regularity, boundary behavior near the axes of the domain as well as long-range and eventual periodicity asymptotics. Notably, smoothness of the solution up to the boundaries depends on compatibility conditions between initial, boundary and forcing data, into which interjected now are initial values of the coefficients. Further results pertaining to solution uniqueness, analyticity and controllability of the addressed problems are thence deduced in light of the preceding qualitative theory.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Chatziafratis, Spyridon Kamvissis, Alain Miranville, Tohru Ozawa

item.title: A Liouville theorem for plurisubharmonic functions with periodic complex Monge-Amp\`ere measure
item.description: arXiv:2610.40004v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study entire continuous plurisubharmonic solutions of the complex Monge-Amp\`ere equation $(i\partial\bar\partial u)^n=2^n n!\mu$ in $\mathbb{C}^n$, in the Bedford-Taylor sense, where $\mu\not\equiv 0$ is a nonnegative locally finite Borel measure periodic with respect to a lattice of full real rank. We assume that $\mu$ is locally dominated by complex Monge-Amp\`ere measures of H\"older continuous plurisubharmonic functions, a condition under which the existence theorem of Demailly et al. yields H\"older continuous periodic correctors. Under this assumption, we prove that every such solution with positive two-sided quadratic growth can be written uniquely, up to an additive constant, as the sum of a real quadratic polynomial and a H\"older continuous periodic function.
item.dc:creator: Jingchen Hu, Xushan Tu

item.title: Holomorphic 1-forms without zeros on K\"ahler manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.40097v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Assuming the existence of good minimal models, we give a bimeromorphic classification of compact connected K\"ahler manifolds admitting a holomorphic 1-form without zeros.
item.dc:creator: Simon Pietig

item.title: Characterizations of Toeplitz operators on the annulus
item.description: arXiv:2610.40118v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish algebraic characterizations of Toeplitz operators on the Hardy space on the annulus. As an application, we characterize compact perturbations of Toeplitz operators.
item.dc:creator: Shubham Jain, Jaydeb Sarkar

item.title: Compact and Hilbert-Schmidt composition operators on weighted Hardy spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.40148v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Lef\`evre, Li, Queff\'elec, and Rodr\'iguez-Piazza [12] recently characterized the sequences $\beta$ for which the weighted Hardy space $H^2(\beta)$ has the same bounded composition operators as the Hardy space $H^2$. We investigate the analogous questions for the compactness and the $p$-Schatten classes: for which sequences $\beta$ does the space $H^2(\beta)$ have the same compact or $p$-Schatten class composition operators as $H^2$?
item.dc:creator: Francisco J. Cruz-Zamorano, Eugenio Dellepiane, Daniel Seco

item.title: Gromov-Witten Generating Series of Elliptic Curves and Iterated Integrals of Eisenstein-Kronecker Forms
item.description: arXiv:2310.08018v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compute various types of iterated integrals of Eisenstein-Kronecker forms that are constructed from the Kronecker theta function. Furthermore, we relate the generating series of Gromov-Witten invariants of elliptic curves to these iterated integrals.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Communications in Number Theory and Physics, Vol. 20, Issue 2 (2026), pp. 309-351
item.dc:creator: Jie Zhou

item.title: Thompson's groups and Teichm\"uller modular groups of generalized Cantor sets
item.description: arXiv:2605.10143v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Thompson's groups, which are denoted by $F, T$ and $V$, were introduced by R. Thompson. It is known that they are related to various fields in mathematics. In this paper, we discuss Thompson's groups $F, T$ and $V$ in Teichm\"uller modular groups of Teichm\"uller spaces of generalized Cantor sets with certain conditions by using a quasiconformal geometric method. Moreover, we show that groups corresponding to $F$ and $T$ act properly discontinuously on such Teichm\"uller spaces. We also show the same results for the asymptotic Teichm\"uller space. E. de Faria, F. P. Gardiner and W. J. Harvey show similar results on Thompson's group $F$ and asymptotic Teichm\"uller spaces. So, our results are improvement of them. We also discuss the actions of Thompson's groups on other spaces which we call \lq\lq pre-Tiechm\"uller spaces" of generalized Cantor sets. Especially, we show that the action of a group which is isomorphic to Thompson's group $V$ on the pre-Teich\"uller space is not properly discontinuous while groups isomorphic to $F$ and $T$ act properly discontinuously. Finally, we construct infinitely many distinct Teichm\"uller spaces of generalized Cantor sets where our results can apply.
item.dc:creator: Hiroshige Shiga

item.title: Spectrum of Complete K\"ahler Metrics on Bounded Hyperconvex Domains
item.description: arXiv:2607.03036v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{C}^{n}$ be a bounded domain, and let $\rho:\Omega\to[-1,0)$ be a smooth strictly plurisubharmonic exhaustion function. We consider the logarithmic potential $g=-\log(-\rho)$ and the associated complete K\"ahler metric $\omega=dd^{c} g$. We prove that if $\rho$ satisfies the finite weighted Monge-Amp\`ere mass condition with weight $(-\rho)^{\varepsilon}$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, then the spectrum and the essential spectrum of the Laplace-Beltrami operator of $(\Omega,\omega)$ both coincide with $[n^{2},\infty)$. In particular, the bottom of the spectrum satisfies $\lambda_{0}(\Delta_{\omega},\Omega)=n^{2}$, and $n^{2}$ is not an $L^{2}$-eigenvalue. For each $\alpha > \frac{n}{2}$, we set $f=(-\rho)^{\alpha}$ and prove that $f$ belongs to $W^{1,2}(\Omega,\omega)$ if and only if the Monge-Amp\`ere mass of $\rho$ weighted by $(-\rho)^{2\alpha-n}$ is finite. The integral identities underlying this equivalence, applied to the complex powers $(-\rho)^{\alpha+it}$, give, after normalization, a singular Weyl sequence at every $n^{2}+4t^{2}$, $t\in\mathbb{R}$, as $\alpha\downarrow\frac{n}{2}$. Combining our theorem with Cegrell's finite-mass exhaustion theorem, we obtain a complete K\"ahler metric with spectrum and essential spectrum equal to $[n^{2},\infty)$ on every bounded hyperconvex domain.
item.dc:creator: Young-Jun Choi, Jiwon Brandon Jeong

item.title: Right $q$-Radial Calculus at Integral Superdimension
item.description: arXiv:2607.14449v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the intrinsic right $q$-radial derivative at integral superdimension $M=m-2n$, using an independent formal parameter $Q$ before the specialisation $Q=q^M$. The exterior-blade action carries the parity factor $(-1)^{|I|}$, and the corresponding Fischer theory uses right multiplication. We establish finite-support compatibility, faithful coordinate realisations in a sufficient finite-block range, and localised Green and determinant-localised Fischer decompositions. For one vector, we determine the kernel and cokernel explicitly, including the additional singular monomial and missing image exactly when $M\in-2\mathbb N_0$. In degree zero the right Fischer operator is diagonal on auxiliary exterior blades, with eigenvalue $[M-p]_q+p$ at nonempty support rank $p$. For positive integral $M$, resonances in $0<q<1$ occur exactly at ranks $p>M$: each rank has one simple resonance, these values increase strictly with $p$, and the corresponding kernels and singular right-monogenic elements are explicit. The two-vector Fischer determinant is nonzero for positive $M$ and $0<q<1$.
item.dc:creator: Juan Bory-Reyes, Baruch Schneider, Diana Barseghyan Schneiderov\'a, Yifan Zhang

item.title: Three omitted values and non-Blaschke point divisors in half-planes
item.description: arXiv:2608.26062v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a real meromorphic function $F$ on $\mathbb C$ such that $F^{-1}(\{0,1,\infty\})\subset\mathbb R$, while $F$ is not of bounded type in either half-plane. More strongly, for every $a\in\widehat{\mathbb C}\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$, the $a$-point divisor in either half-plane fails the Blaschke condition. Thus the construction gives a negative answer to the half-plane bounded-type question arising from Nevanlinna's 1925 work. Postcomposition gives the analogous counterexample for any prescribed triple of distinct values in the Riemann sphere. The core construction and proof were generated during an autonomous run of GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra.
item.dc:creator: Quanyu Tang, Bokai Cui, Wei He, Tao Hu, Yanyang Li, Ke Wang, Zijun Yu

item.title: Radii of Starlikeness of Spirallike Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.06175v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A normalized analytic function $f$ defined on the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$ is called $\alpha$-spirallike if $f(\mathbb{D})$ is an $\alpha$-spirallike domain, that is, for every $z\in f(\mathbb{D})$, the $\alpha$-spiral $ze^{-e^{i\alpha}t}$, $t\ge0$, is contained in $f(\mathbb{D})$, or equivalently, if $\operatorname{Re}\!\left(e^{i\alpha} {zf'(z)}/{f(z)}\right)>0$ for all $z\in \mathbb{D}$. The 0-spirallike functions are the usual starlike functions. The function $f$ is parabolic starlike, if $\operatorname{Re}\!\left(\frac{zf'(z)}{f(z)}\right)>\left|\frac{zf'(z)}{f(z)}-1\right|$, and lemniscate starlike if $|(zf'(z)/f(z))^2-1|<1$ respectively. In this paper, we determine the radii of parabolic starlikeness and lemniscate starlikeness of $\alpha$-spirallike functions. Our approach combines geometric characterizations of the underlying regions with the resultant method for eliminating auxiliary variables, leading to explicit equations for the sharp radii. Some known radius results are recovered as special cases.
item.dc:creator: Lakshmipriya Arul, Vaithiyanathan Ravichandran

item.title: Criteria for a fiberwise Fujiki/Kahler family to be locally Moishezon/projective
item.description: arXiv:2503.07548v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we utilize the theory of non-K\"ahler loci by S. Boucksom to construct an integral $2$-cohomology class whose restriction to a general fiber is big, and then construct a relatively big line bundle via the exponential sequence. This leads to a local Moishezonness criterion for fibrations whose total spaces are compact complex manifolds in the Fujiki class $\mathscr{C}$, generalizing the bimeromorphic version of F. Campana's local projectivity theorem. We further combine a similar idea with the singular Demailly--P\u{a}un theorem by T. Collins--V. Tosatti to obtain a local projectivity criterion for fibrations from compact K\"ahler manifolds, yielding a new proof and a generalization of F. Campana's local projectivity theorem.
item.dc:creator: Jian Chen

item.title: On the hyperplane conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.26186v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the hyperplane conjecture, proposed by Hosono, Lian, and Yau in arXiv:alg-geom/9511001, for Batyrev's mirror pairs of Calabi--Yau hypersurfaces and its orbifold generalization, without assuming that the lattice points in the defining reflexive polytope generate the ambient lattice. We then identify the pushforward of the extended hypersurface \(I\)-function with a generating series of normalized compact periods of the mirror, providing a period interpretation of the hypergeometric series governing ambient genus-zero orbifold Gromov--Witten theory. As an application of our method, we also identify the residue of the Gauss--Manin connection and the cup product morphism on the \(A\)-side.
item.dc:creator: Tsung-Ju Lee

item.title: The Beurling-type theorem for powers of weighted Bergman shifts
item.description: arXiv:2610.37035v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal{B}_{\alpha}$ denote the shift operator on the weighted Bergman space $A^2_\alpha(\mathbb{D})$. We prove that, for every integer $k\geq1$, the Beurling-type theorem holds for $\mathcal{B}_{\alpha}^k$ on $A^2_\alpha(\mathbb{D})$ if and only if $-1<\alpha\leq1$. We also show that, for every $\alpha>-1$, there exists a finite Blaschke product $B$ such that $M_{B}$ admits a cyclic invariant subspace but fails the wandering subspace property.
item.dc:creator: Shibo Xu, Tao Yu
